summary.text: Youngest and comeliest daughter of great-hearted Eurymedon, once king over the insolent Giants — by Poseidon she bore Nausithous, founder of the Phaeacian line on Scheria.

story.text: Homer names her only in the genealogy of the Phaeacian kings. Eurymedon ruled the insolent Giants and brought destruction on his froward people; with his youngest daughter Periboea lay Poseidon, and she bore a son, great-hearted Nausithous, who ruled over the Phaeacians and begat Rhexenor and Alcinous before he himself perished.

Through this union the sea-god enters the royal house of Scheria: Nausithous is counted godlike, and his removal of the Phaeacians from Hypereia to their walled city on Corcyra is the work of a founder sprung from the earth-shaker and a princess of the ruined Giant-kings.
